initializer.description: Null operand or absent name callback returns null. Otherwise invokes the actual registered actor-name callback and retains its reference record itself. It does not dereference the first-pointer world object. The cached reference persists when primary-player globals later change.

IAm.description: Null script creature or null creature+0xd0 reference returns float0. Exact equality between the reference and cached initializer result returns float1 before definition/name checks. Otherwise the reference+0x54 definition and its+0xc name must be nonnull; whole case-insensitive equality to the condition operand returns1, else0. It does not compare the world object, actor display name, type-group slot or current player ownership. Operand null gives no name match but can still pass cached pointer identity.

coverage.description: All138 shipped IAm operands run through original initializer/callback/predicate in four contexts: unmatched/default, matching definition with bound identity, matching definition without callback, and absent creature. Targeted cases add null operand/reference/definition/name, stale binding after changed player globals, world-object/reference differences and explicit mismatching cached references. Predicate return is captured directly from x87 into float32. Script comparators/connectives are outside this small predicate suite and remain governed by the existing scheduler contracts.

verification.method: Original initializer0x515730, actual registered callback0x43c220 and predicate0x515750 execute unchanged. Predicate x87 return is captured to float32; only bounded CRT Player%d formatting is substituted.

adapters: Reference/definition attachment, cached identity lifetime and current world/player tables are supplied data.
Native initializer uses the recovered ActorStateWorld.FindReference algorithm; only bounded CRT Player%d is substituted in native fixtures.

remaining: Valid runtime reference identity and definitions; record allocation/lifetime are supplied.
ASCII operand/name comparisons; cached pointer identity persists across later player-global changes.
Core/replay compile only; no generated managed executable launch.
